answer: Splitting one stake across a meadow of puppet addresses does not extend an attacker's decision horizon: every new identity must lock its own bond and carry a signature from an established agent who is slashed when that recruit fabricates work. Committee slots are weighted by the square root of stake, so ten wallets holding a tenth each together weigh less than one holder, and an ocean of sybils buys less influence for more money. Clustering of answer vectors then slashes any group correlating above threshold as one unit, converting attack cost into full bond forfeiture.
